# Beacon — full documentation summary for language models

> Beacon is a free, MIT-licensed family command center for wall-mounted displays, and a self-hosted alternative to Skylight Calendar, Hearth Display, and DAKboard. Install it as a one-click Home Assistant add-on, or run it standalone with Docker. It runs in any tablet's browser, or as a signed Android APK sideloaded from GitHub releases (it is not on the Play Store, and there is no iOS build). The dashboard includes a calendar with month and week views, chores, grocery lists, weather, a photo screensaver, custom fonts and themes, Kid Display, kiosk mode, and multiple languages. There is an in-app meal planner with a week grid for breakfast, lunch, dinner, and snacks (it follows Settings → General → Week Starts On) and an editable dashboard Menu card (including on empty days). Meals can use a Beacon recipe. Add ingredients to grocery list writes to the default list or the built-in Shopping List, including Home Assistant to-do lists, not Grocy. The MCP tool beacon_set_meal_plan merges by default; a null or empty name clears one slot, and replace: true restores the old replace-everything behavior. You can still fill the plan from an AnyList sync. Google Photos support works through pasted shared-album links, which the server caches and refreshes every 6 hours; that path relies on an unofficial Google page format. You can also use any Home Assistant media folder as a photo source.

- Docs: __SITE_URL__
- Compact index: __SITE_URL__/llms.txt
- Source: https://github.com/asachs01/beacon
- Releases (including the Android APK): https://github.com/asachs01/beacon/releases
- Home Assistant community thread: https://community.home-assistant.io/t/beacon-free-family-command-center-add-on/1000220
- Getting help: questions and setup help go to [Discussions Q&A](https://github.com/asachs01/beacon/discussions/categories/q-a); feature ideas go to [Discussions Ideas](https://github.com/asachs01/beacon/discussions/categories/ideas); share your setup in [Show your setup](https://github.com/asachs01/beacon/discussions/categories/show-your-setup); bug reports go to [GitHub issues](https://github.com/asachs01/beacon/issues). The Home Assistant community thread above is an additional place to talk about the add-on.

Docs links use the current docs origin; paths stay the same if the host changes.

## What Beacon is not

- Not a hosted or subscription product. There is no Beacon cloud account.
- Not on the Apple App Store or Google Play. Android is a signed APK from GitHub releases, sideloaded. There is no iOS build.
- Not an official Google Photos integration. Shared-album links are read from Google's public share page, which is unofficial and can change. If a refresh fails, Beacon keeps the last cached photos and shows a warning in Settings.

## Install and setup

### Getting Started
URL: __SITE_URL__/docs/getting-started/installation/

Install Beacon as a Home Assistant add-on (add the GitHub repo as an add-on repository, then install and start Beacon), as a standalone Docker container, or as a local development server. From [v1.50.1](https://github.com/asachs01/beacon/releases/tag/v1.50.1), a standalone Docker container connects to Home Assistant when you set `HA_URL` (the base Home Assistant address, with no `/api`) and `HA_TOKEN` (a long-lived access token). Do not set `SUPERVISOR_TOKEN` when running standalone; add-on users see no change. You can also run without Home Assistant, with calendars, lists, and tasks stored in the browser. See [Deployment](__SITE_URL__/docs/getting-started/deployment/). From [v1.54.0](https://github.com/asachs01/beacon/releases/tag/v1.54.0), a device that opens Beacon directly on its port pairs once. See [Pairing a device](__SITE_URL__/docs/getting-started/pairing/).

### Deployment
URL: __SITE_URL__/docs/getting-started/deployment/

Covers Home Assistant add-on vs standalone Docker (`HA_URL` and `HA_TOKEN` from [v1.50.1](https://github.com/asachs01/beacon/releases/tag/v1.50.1); do not set `SUPERVISOR_TOKEN` when standalone), reverse proxy, hardware recommendations, kiosk mode on a wall tablet, and performance notes. From [v1.54.0](https://github.com/asachs01/beacon/releases/tag/v1.54.0), a device that opens Beacon directly on its port pairs once. See [Pairing a device](__SITE_URL__/docs/getting-started/pairing/).

### Pairing a device
URL: __SITE_URL__/docs/getting-started/pairing/

From [v1.54.0](https://github.com/asachs01/beacon/releases/tag/v1.54.0). A device that opens Beacon directly on its port (Docker, standalone, or a hand-mapped add-on port) pairs once with the family PIN or a 6-digit code. Opening Beacon from the Home Assistant sidebar, and the Android app's built-in dashboard, do not pair. `HA_BROWSER_TOKEN` is ignored. Automations and `rest_command`s send `Authorization: !secret beacon_token` (the add-on writes it to `secrets.yaml` automatically; on standalone, create one under Settings → Devices → Create access token and add it before restarting Home Assistant). Settings → Devices has Rotate pairing code. From [v1.54.3](https://github.com/asachs01/beacon/releases/tag/v1.54.3), the public `runtime-config.js` file contains the family name, theme, and auto dark mode setting; it never contains a token. Update to [v1.54.3](https://github.com/asachs01/beacon/releases/tag/v1.54.3) or later. Advisory: [GHSA-rj98-fx8p-896h](https://github.com/asachs01/beacon/security/advisories/GHSA-rj98-fx8p-896h).

### Android app
URL: __SITE_URL__/docs/getting-started/android/

Each GitHub release attaches a signed APK (`beacon-vX.Y.Z.apk`) and a SHA-256 checksum. Sideload the APK, verify the checksum, and point the app at your Home Assistant URL. This is not a Play Store listing. There is no iOS app.

### Updating and Troubleshooting
URL: __SITE_URL__/docs/getting-started/updating/

From v1.43.2, add-on updates download a prebuilt multi-arch image from `ghcr.io/asachs01/beacon` instead of building on the Home Assistant device. The first update after 1.43.2 swaps a locally built image for the published one; existing settings carry over. The page also covers rollbacks, logs, stale browser caches after an update, kiosk exits, and other common fixes.

## Features

### Calendar
URL: __SITE_URL__/docs/features/calendar/

Month and week views, creating and editing events, recurring events, and drag-to-reschedule. Calendars typically come from Home Assistant calendar entities.

### Chores
URL: __SITE_URL__/docs/features/chores/

Assign chores, track streaks, and show a family leaderboard. Chores can have dollar values for a weekly earnings view.

### Chore privileges
URL: __SITE_URL__/docs/features/chore-privileges/

Optional per-child Home Assistant entity (switch, input_boolean, light, or fan) that turns on when today's assigned chores are complete and off when they are not, including when the chore day rolls at the daily reset time (local midnight when that time is unset). The add-on also fires `beacon_chore_completed` and `beacon_all_chores_done`. Standalone mode does not fire those events. Existing members are unchanged until a parent sets the switch.

### Press-to-talk
URL: __SITE_URL__/docs/features/press-to-talk/

Hold-to-talk on the wall display. There is no wake word and the microphone is not always on. When a Home Assistant conversation agent is available in add-on mode, the utterance goes to `conversation.process`. Otherwise it goes to `POST /beacon-action/voice`. The reply shows in an overlay that dismisses itself. "Mark dishes as done" completes the chore in FamilyStore (not `todo.chores`), fires the same chore events, and re-evaluates privilege switches. An ambiguous title asks which chore or which person. Adding a grocery item uses the existing todo list path. "What's on the calendar today" reads today's events. "What chores are left" reads today's remaining chores from Beacon's chart, and a person's name limits that list. It does not read `todo.chores`. The Voice button setting is on by default in the add-on and off in a standalone browser until enabled. The mic needs HTTPS or localhost; Home Assistant ingress over HTTPS works, and a plain HTTP kiosk keeps the text box. Checking a chore by voice does not ask for a PIN.

### Magic Import
URL: __SITE_URL__/docs/features/magic-import/

Text import shipped in [v1.47.0](https://github.com/asachs01/beacon/releases/tag/v1.47.0). Photo and PDF import shipped in [v1.49.0](https://github.com/asachs01/beacon/releases/tag/v1.49.0). You can paste a school email or other text, or add one photo or PDF (JPEG, PNG, HEIC where the browser can convert it, or PDF; one file, 10 MB). Review the draft events and list items, and approve them with the family PIN. Pasted text, and a PDF with real text (read in the browser, first 5 pages), is processed by your Home Assistant conversation agent, or a local parser. If that agent is a cloud service (OpenAI, Google, or Anthropic), Home Assistant sends the text to that provider. Only photos and scanned PDFs (page 1 of a scan) need the Home Assistant AI Task entity you pick in Settings → Display → Magic Import: AI Task entity for photos (Home Assistant 2025.8 or newer; the picker is empty by default, so photo and scan import stays off until you pick one). The local parser can't read images, and a failed photo read does not fall back to it. If photo and scan import is off, a scanned PDF is not sent to the local parser. Beacon does not write the file to its own /data; it briefly uploads it to Home Assistant's local media source for the task and deletes it afterward. A cloud AI Task sends the file to that provider. The Import screens name the conversation agent or AI Task entity and label it local, cloud, or may be cloud. Settings → Display → Magic Import is on by default in the add-on and off in a standalone browser. Turning off "Magic Import: use Home Assistant conversation agent" forces the local parser for text and turns off photo and scan import; a PDF with real text can still use the local parser. Beacon does not import forwarded email, so this mostly closes the gap with Skylight Calendar's Magic Import, not fully.

### Grocery
URL: __SITE_URL__/docs/features/grocery/

Shopping lists from built-in local lists, Home Assistant to-do entities, or AnyList. From [v1.52.0](https://github.com/asachs01/beacon/releases/tag/v1.52.0), Beacon can also use the HACS Grocy integration (Settings → Integrations → Grocy). Magic Import can add items to Grocy's shopping list through `add_generic`. Optional expiring-products and low-stock dashboard cards (off by default) read `binary_sensor.grocy_expiring_products` and `binary_sensor.grocy_missing_products`; a card stays hidden if its entity is missing. From 1.52.1, with Grocy Integration on, the Grocery screen includes a list named Grocy and check-offs on that list write the shopping-list done flag. The expiring card shows only items due within 3 days. The meal planner's Add ingredients to grocery list still writes to the default list or the built-in Shopping List, including Home Assistant to-do lists, not Grocy.
### Photos
URL: __SITE_URL__/docs/features/photos/

Photo sources include a local `photo_directory`, any Home Assistant media-source folder (useful for Immich, a NAS, or album_slideshow), and Google Photos shared-album links. For Google Photos, paste one or more link-shared album URLs (`https://photos.google.com/share/...`) in Settings > Photos. Beacon's server downloads the pictures into `/data/photo-cache/google/`, refreshes about 15 seconds after startup and then every 6 hours (or when you press Refresh now), and skips videos. This depends on the unofficial HTML of Google's public share page. If a refresh cannot fetch or parse the page, the last successful download stays on the frame and Settings shows a warning with that timestamp.

### Screen Saver
URL: __SITE_URL__/docs/features/screensaver/

A photo screensaver with crossfade transitions and an optional clock overlay.

### Night mode
URL: __SITE_URL__/docs/features/night-mode/

Shipped in [v1.50.0](https://github.com/asachs01/beacon/releases/tag/v1.50.0). Off by default under Settings → Display → Night mode. You can set a schedule (default 9:00 PM to 6:30 AM; overnight ranges work; the schedule uses the device's local time) or turn it on or off manually. The Night mode switch has to be on; a manual override of Schedule, On, or Off cannot enable it by itself. While it is on, Beacon switches to the Midnight theme without rewriting the saved theme, adds a dim layer (default 30%; a CSS overlay, not a change to the device's screen brightness), and can show an optional clock-only screen. A tap removes the dim layer and the clock-only screen for 60 seconds, so the dashboard is back at full brightness, still in the Midnight theme. A finished countdown timer wakes the screen and holds it until the alarm is dismissed, and for at least 60 seconds even if the alarm is dismissed sooner. Shared timers and Family Bell do not yet call this wake hook. Night mode also runs on the Kid Display and kiosk views when it is turned on. The dim overlay does not capture taps, and the hidden corner used to leave kiosk mode or Kid Display stays open, including when Clock only is on.


### Guest mode
URL: __SITE_URL__/docs/features/guest-mode/

Shipped in [v1.51.0](https://github.com/asachs01/beacon/releases/tag/v1.51.0). Optional guest PIN, empty by default, under Settings → Display → Guest mode. A guest enters with the corner gesture plus that PIN, and a Guest badge stays on the screen. Guests can view the calendar, check off chores, add to the grocery list, and use timers. They can view events but cannot create, edit, or delete them, and they cannot change settings or approve imports. What is hidden is a deny-list: whereabouts features (presence and location) and calendars marked Hide from guests are hidden; meals, photos, music, and the leaderboard stay visible. Guest check-offs on a family member's chore earn points and streaks and show "Checked off by Guest" on chore rows (the Chores screen, and completed chore rows on the dashboard and calendar task lists). Home Assistant to-do items don't get the label. From [v1.52.0](https://github.com/asachs01/beacon/releases/tag/v1.52.0), an unassigned guest check-off is recorded as Guest and earns no points. Guests can earn rewards but cannot redeem them. A session ends with the family PIN, the guest PIN when no family PIN is set, the timeout (default 4 hours), or when the guest PIN is cleared or changed. Leaving kiosk or Kid Display is a separate step. Guest mode is not a security boundary: it only limits what this Beacon screen shows.

### Home sensors
URL: __SITE_URL__/docs/features/home-sensors/

Shipped in [v1.53.0](https://github.com/asachs01/beacon/releases/tag/v1.53.0). Off by default. Pick entities under Settings → Integrations (each can have a friendly name and icon), then add the card in dashboard edit mode. It is not in the Family, Classic, or Compact layouts. Values update live over the Home Assistant websocket, with no polling. If an entity is unavailable, unknown, or hasn't updated in 3 hours, the card shows "Unavailable", "Unknown", or "No update in 3 h" instead of a stale value. The card shows only the entities you pick, and it excludes cameras. The card is read-only: it does not toggle devices, call services, or show camera feeds. The `/beacon-ws/ha` server connection only passes `get_states`, `state_changed` subscriptions, `unsubscribe_events` for subscriptions it opened, and `ping`; other commands are refused. Hidden from guests and Kid Display. Works with the add-on and standalone (`HA_URL`/`HA_TOKEN`).

### Meals
URL: __SITE_URL__/docs/features/meals/

Shipped in [v1.48.0](https://github.com/asachs01/beacon/releases/tag/v1.48.0). An in-app meal planner. The Meals sidebar view is a week grid for breakfast, lunch, dinner, and snacks; the grid follows Settings → General → Week Starts On. The dashboard Menu card is editable, including on days with nothing planned. Meals can be named, noted, and tied to a Beacon recipe. Add ingredients to grocery list writes to the default list or the built-in Shopping List, including Home Assistant to-do lists. It does not write to Grocy. The MCP tool `beacon_set_meal_plan` merges by default (upsert by date and meal type; a null or empty name clears that one slot; other dates are left alone). Pass `replace: true` to replace the whole plan, which is the previous behavior. You can still fill the plan with the `scripts/sync-meals.mjs` AnyList sync script. The first rewrite of an existing plan writes a one-time backup: `beacon_meal_plans.bak.json` on the add-on, or `beacon_meal_plans.bak` in local storage in a standalone browser.

### Kid Display Mode
URL: __SITE_URL__/docs/features/kid-display/

A simplified view aimed at children. The docs also cover how to exit it.
